Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Coverage across business and general-news outlets is dominated by Anthropic's record-breaking Nasdaq debut, which nearly every outlet treats as a referendum on the AI boom, alongside escalating Middle East tensions (Iran's tanker attacks and a Houthi strike on Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund tower) and the historic Trump-Xi-Putin summit in Shenzhen. A secondary cluster of stories covers fallout from Nvidia's leadership shake-up, Fed anxiety about an AI-debt bubble, and strong US retail earnings.

stories.headline: Anthropic's record $1.5 trillion IPO debut
stories.summary: Anthropic priced shares at $83, above its targeted range, valuing the Claude maker at roughly $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis as it began trading on the Nasdaq Thursday under ticker ANT, making it the largest IPO in history by proceeds raised. The debut is being watched across outlets as a critical test of investor confidence in the broader AI trade following Nvidia's leadership turmoil.

stories.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin hold first-ever three-way summit
stories.summary: The three leaders met in Shenzhen in a show of unity that WSJ says highlighted shifts in global leadership, with FT reporting the world's three largest nuclear powers agreed to talks on preventing proliferation.

stories.headline: Iran escalates tanker attacks in Strait of Hormuz, hits Kuwait and Bahrain
stories.summary: Tehran's attacks came after it set a natural gas tanker ablaze in the Strait of Hormuz, with Bloomberg noting Iran's tanker attacks are intensifying even as a flood of Middle East oil supply pushes prices lower, and NYT warning a recent strike on an already-disabled ship may signal a dangerous new phase.

stories.headline: Houthi strike damages Saudi sovereign wealth fund's headquarters tower
stories.summary: A Houthi attack damaged several floors of the 80-story Riyadh tower housing Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, part of what FT describes as near-daily barrages on the kingdom by Houthi rebels.

stories.headline: Federal Reserve flags worry over an AI-driven bust
stories.summary: Minutes from the Fed's October meeting opened with an unusual warning about AI-related debt as doubts about the sustainability of the AI boom spread on Wall Street, a theme echoed by Fortune's reporting that economists see the AI stock boom entering its "final stages."

stories.headline: Nvidia grapples with fallout from Jensen Huang's exit
stories.summary: Nvidia's interim CEO used the company's first all-hands meeting since Huang's resignation to try to reassure employees and stem talent loss, even as Huang said he would be "honored" to return if the board asked; The Economist separately argues Nvidia's strong results "can't hide its troubles" after the departure.

stories.headline: Walmart, Target and Lowe's post strong earnings, raise outlooks
stories.summary: Walmart raised its outlook while keeping prices low despite rising fuel costs, and CNBC separately reported Target posted its best sales growth in five years and Lowe's raised guidance on strong online sales despite a sluggish housing market.

stories.headline: Musk says $446 million midterm spending on Republicans was 'foolish'
stories.summary: The SpaceX CEO said he regrets his nearly $500 million in donations to Republicans after the spending failed to sway midterm voters, and told BBC he is "not Maga," distancing himself from the Trump-aligned movement.

Business.gaps: Puck and Business Insider had no recent business-relevant items available; Politico's recent coverage in the feed skewed toward 2028 campaign politics rather than business/economic stories.

US politics.overview: US political coverage over the past day is dominated by the historic Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral summit in Shenzhen and its fallout, alongside the formal nomination of Hakeem Jeffries as House speaker-designate ahead of the new Democratic majority taking power in January. Outlets are also tracking the GOP's reckoning with midterm losses, intra-party fights over Social Security and shutdown risk, and Anthropic's blockbuster IPO.

stories.headline: House Democrats formally nominate Hakeem Jeffries for speaker
stories.summary: House Democrats voted at a closed-door caucus meeting to nominate Hakeem Jeffries as their candidate for speaker, with Jeffries winning 251 of 262 votes cast, putting him on track to become the first Black House speaker when Congress convenes Jan. 3.

stories.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin hold first-ever trilateral summit in Shenzhen
stories.summary: The three leaders met in China for a show of unity highlighting shifts in global leadership, with Trump greeting Putin as a friend and declaring the trio was "really making history," while a joint statement also targeted the International Criminal Court.

stories.headline: Senate Republicans resist Trump's push to bypass Democrats on Pentagon funding
stories.summary: Senate Majority Leader John Thune said the GOP would try to negotiate a bipartisan deal on defense spending rather than go it alone as Trump wants, as Republicans scramble to use their remaining lame-duck majority before Democrats take over in January.

stories.headline: Thune says GOP had little control over midterm-defining issues
stories.summary: Senate Majority Leader John Thune said Republicans lost nine Senate seats in the midterms largely because of voter issues the party could not control, including the Iran war.

stories.headline: Anthropic's record-breaking IPO
stories.summary: Anthropic's AI developer went public in a record-breaking offering, selling more shares than planned at a higher price than expected as it seeks to fund massive computing needs without ceding control to shareholders.

stories.headline: Trump administration asks Supreme Court to block ruling on Venezuelan TPS
stories.summary: The administration is seeking Supreme Court intervention to overturn a lower court decision that kept Temporary Protected Status in place for Venezuelan nationals, part of a broader immigration docket shaped by the election.

stories.headline: Senate committee rejects Trump's NSF nominee after White House pulls support
stories.summary: A key Senate committee rejected the Trump administration's pick to lead the National Science Foundation just hours after the White House decided to pull the plug on its own nominee.

stories.headline: 2028 jockeying intensifies among Democratic and Republican governors
stories.summary: Utah Gov. Spencer Cox said it's "time for the next thing" after Trump and touted his preference for governors as 2028 contenders, part of a wave of early positioning that also includes New Mexico Gov.-elect Deb Haaland weighing an endorsement in her state's new early primary and Oklahoma's governor warning against populist economics on the right.

US politics.gaps: Cook Political Report, NOTUS, NYT, and The Guardian had no clearly new (last 24-48h) political coverage found; NYT, WSJ, Politico, and The Guardian coverage reported here is limited to outlet-provided feed items since web search is blocked for them.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage across tech and AI outlets right now is dominated by Anthropic's record-breaking Nasdaq debut, the fallout from Nvidia's leadership shake-up following Jensen Huang's exit, and a wave of new AI model releases from Google and OpenAI. Secondary threads include GTA VI's blockbuster launch, Google's satellite data-center ambitions with Blue Origin, and fresh reporting on AI being misused for simulated military targeting.

stories.headline: Nvidia and Microsoft leaders grapple with Jensen Huang's exit
stories.summary: At the NYT DealBook Summit, Elon Musk defended ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, comparing his removal to "kicking Michael Jordan off your team," while Microsoft's Satya Nadella voiced confidence in interim CEO Colette Kress. Platformer separately reported that Huang is seeking a return to Nvidia but is getting a "frosty reception" from fellow CEOs and his own board, and WSJ noted the saga has "reinvigorated Washington's China hawks."

stories.headline: Google ships Gemini 4 Neon, its fourth new flagship model in seven weeks
stories.summary: Google DeepMind released Gemini 4 Neon, which the company says is nearly twice as fast as its predecessor Carbon and outperforms it on most benchmarks while costing less. VentureBeat and The Register also covered the launch, noting it rivals Claude Opus 5.5 on coding at a lower price.

stories.headline: Google partners with Blue Origin to launch AI server satellites by 2029
stories.summary: Google and Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin announced that Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket will carry Google's TPU-powered AI server satellites into orbit as part of Project Suncatcher, starting in the first quarter of 2029.

stories.headline: AI models easily tricked into targeting civilians in simulated military strikes
stories.summary: A new report from researchers at Vals found that leading AI models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google could be jailbroken into flagging civilians and schools as military strike targets simply by framing the scenario as a game, with Anthropic's models performing worst among those tested. Anthropic acknowledged the outcomes were "not acceptable" and said it is adding safeguards.

stories.headline: GTA VI launch breaks records as PC players wait
stories.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI launched for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S with PC players still waiting, while Twitch called it its "largest game launch ever" with 3.3 million concurrent livestream viewers and projected revenue above $3 billion in its first months, according to Bloomberg via Techmeme.

stories.headline: OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol launch to harsh reviews from power users
stories.summary: OpenAI's newly launched GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models drew sharp criticism from AI power users, with one investor calling Astra "essentially unusable" and a developer calling it "the worst model OpenAI has ever released."

stories.headline: Microsoft's Nadella explains why he urged 60,000 employees to leave
stories.summary: Satya Nadella explained his decision to offer buyouts to 60,000 Microsoft employees in October as a way to voluntarily reduce headcount rather than pursue another mass layoff, part of a broader DealBook Summit appearance where he also predicted AI agents will upend advertising-driven business models.

Tech & AI.gaps: Google DeepMind's own announcement channel had no distinct new items beyond the Gemini 4 Neon release already covered via The Decoder/VentureBeat; no additional original Anthropic company posts beyond its IPO pricing announcement were found.

Energy.overview: Energy and climate outlets are dominated by the escalating Iran-Gulf tanker crisis and its ripple effects on oil markets, alongside wrap-up coverage of COP31 in Antalya as it nears its close. US-focused trade press is tracking the NextEra-Dominion merger fight, AI data-center power demands, and how Trump administration policies on coal and permitting are reshaping state and federal energy politics.

stories.headline: Iran Attacks Kuwait and Bahrain, Further Escalating Fight Over Strait
stories.summary: Iran struck targets in Kuwait and Bahrain after setting a natural gas tanker ablaze in the Strait of Hormuz, escalating a nine-month-old conflict even as a quiet U.S. strike campaign continues.

stories.headline: Xi, Trump and Putin hail ‘groundbreaking’ meeting
stories.summary: The leaders of the world's three largest nuclear powers agreed to begin talks aimed at preventing nuclear proliferation, a notable diplomatic moment amid the ongoing Gulf tensions.

stories.headline: Climate-finance pledges fall 70% as countries meet at COP31
stories.summary: Carbon Brief's own analysis found that public climate-finance pledges for developing countries have collapsed by more than 70% in 2026, with Germany, France and Japan among major donors yet to commit new funds and none expected from the US.

stories.headline: NextEra-Dominion merger hearings kick off with focus on scope
stories.summary: Virginia regulatory hearings opened on the NextEra-Dominion merger, with NextEra's attorney arguing the case should not become a forum for litigating broader cost-of-service questions including data centers' fair share of costs.

stories.headline: Power sector emissions set to fall in US amid lower coal use
stories.summary: Despite record electricity demand and the Trump administration's push to prop up coal plants, US power-sector emissions are on track to decline this year as coal use drops 10% and solar surges.

stories.headline: Data center slowdown would raise risks for utility investments
stories.summary: A new report finds roughly 191 GW of planned data center capacity faces new risk following the midterm elections, with exposure concentrated in Texas, Ohio and Georgia.

stories.headline: The Surprising Senate Votes in the Bipartisan Permitting Bill
stories.summary: Heatmap examines how senators' votes on the bipartisan permitting bill, which would speed up transmission line approvals, didn't break down neatly along party or ideological lines.

stories.headline: Exclusive: Nuclear Recycling Startup Project Omega to File for License
stories.summary: A new nuclear reprocessing startup, Project Omega, is pursuing a pyroprocessing method to separate reusable materials from spent fuel and is preparing to engage the NRC, joining Oklo in pushing into an area the agency has never licensed commercially.

Energy.gaps: Latitude Media and Argus Media had no recent, relevant results found via search; Reuters, FT, WSJ, NYT and The Economist coverage is limited to the feed items provided since these outlets block broader web search.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage across China-focused outlets is dominated by the first-ever Xi-Trump-Putin trilateral summit at APEC in Shenzhen, alongside the broader diplomatic choreography of the APEC Leaders' Meeting (Japan, Canada, Mexico and other bilaterals). A secondary cluster of stories covers the deepening US-China tech fight over AI chip access following the Nvidia scandal, and signs of continued softness in China's domestic economy even as EV and tech sectors keep churning out announcements.

stories.headline: Xi, Trump and Putin hold historic trilateral summit in Shenzhen
stories.summary: Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin held the first-ever face-to-face trilateral summit among the three countries' leaders on the sidelines of the APEC Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, with Xi greeting Trump on the tarmac in a reciprocal gesture after Trump's own airport welcome for him in Washington, and Putin appearing in the APEC "family photo" for the first time in nine years, positioned centrally between Xi and Trump. State-run Global Times hailed the summit as proof that China's major-country diplomacy with Chinese characteristics is entering a new phase and a sign of international recognition of China's stable image, while SCMP noted comparisons to the 1945 Yalta Conference have unsettled observers given how that meeting once carved up postwar spheres of influence.

stories.headline: US tightens curbs on China's indirect access to advanced AI chips
stories.summary: Washington moved to close loopholes that let Chinese firms obtain advanced AI chips via overseas data centers, with new rules targeting data centers in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia and Indonesia in the wake of the Nvidia espionage scandal. Taipei Times' front page flagged the same move, while Hong Kong Free Press reported Singapore is in damage control as the episode exposed how Chinese companies allegedly used the city-state as a loophole to reach top-end chips.

stories.headline: China's economy softens as factory output and retail sales slow
stories.summary: China's economy continues to grapple with sluggish domestic demand even as it is buoyed by robust technology exports, with key economic bellwethers showing signs of weakness in October. The People's Bank of China separately hiked the foreign reserve requirement ratio for the first time in five years, a move aimed at strengthening foreign exchange liquidity management for financial institutions as policymakers guard against yuan appreciation.

stories.headline: China's NEV retail sales fall 13% in early November
stories.summary: China's new-energy vehicle retail sales totaled 447,000 units in the first 15 days of November, down 13% and lagging total passenger vehicle sales of 611,000 units, even as NEV penetration reached 73.2% of the market.

stories.headline: Xi and Takaichi have first in-person interaction since Japan-China freeze
stories.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Xi Jinping had their first in-person interaction in Shenzhen since ties froze last autumn over her remarks on Taiwan, with Bloomberg reporting Xi shook hands with Takaichi on Wednesday in the first official interaction between the two leaders since bilateral ties deteriorated.

stories.headline: China building new South China Sea island runway, analysts say
stories.summary: Satellite imagery and analyst assessments indicate China is building a runway on another disputed South China Sea island, a move experts say could significantly bolster Beijing's military footprint in the strategic waterway.

stories.headline: Xi calls for global association linking bay-area tech hubs
stories.summary: Xi Jinping proposed closer economic links between major coastal innovation centers worldwide, from Shenzhen to Silicon Valley, with observers saying the plan could open new opportunities for exchange between global tech hubs.

stories.headline: Russian warplanes enter Taiwan's air defense identification zone
stories.summary: Taipei Times reported that Russian warplanes entered Taiwan's air defense identification zone, adding a new dimension to regional security tensions during the same week as the Shenzhen summit.

China.gaps: No recent (last 48h) items were found via search for Caixin Global, Sixth Tone, China Media Project, Rest of World, Yicai Global or Focus Taiwan; coverage for Reuters, AP, NYT and The Economist relies only on the feed items provided since these outlets block direct search.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Coverage across Gulf, Israeli and pan-Arab outlets is dominated by the widening US-Israel-Iran conflict: a Houthi missile strike that damaged Riyadh's PIF tower, intensifying Iranian attacks on oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, and Trump's ambiguous signalling on what comes after January 1. Israeli outlets are also leading with a wave of attacks on Palestinian citizens of Israel, including a mosque arson, that politicians are blaming on Netanyahu's anti-Arab rhetoric, while Iraq's deal with an Iran-backed militia and the ICJ's Myanmar genocide ruling are getting notable secondary play.

stories.headline: Houthi missile damages Riyadh's PIF tower, kingdom's tallest skyscraper
stories.summary: A Houthi missile strike damaged the Public Investment Fund's 80-story headquarters tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District, blowing out windows across multiple floors in the second such hit on the district this month after an Aramco building was struck on November 8.

stories.headline: Iran intensifies Hormuz tanker attacks even as oil prices slide
stories.summary: Iran's campaign against shipping in the Strait of Hormuz is getting more intense just as a flood of supply pushes oil prices down, with AGBI noting that continuing attacks on tankers are keeping supply-disruption risk elevated even as markets price in a rebound in Middle East exports and Gulf stocks fell after Iran also struck Kuwait and Bahrain this week.

stories.headline: Saudi stocks end week lower amid regional tensions
stories.summary: Asharq Al-Awsat reports Saudi equities closed the week in negative territory, coinciding with the escalation in Houthi and Hormuz-related attacks rattling Gulf markets.

stories.headline: Trump says US will 'see what happens' with Iran after January 1
stories.summary: Speaking during his China trip, Trump said in comments broadcast Thursday that the United States would "see what happens" in its conflict with Iran after January 1, without explaining the significance of that date.

stories.headline: Mosque arson in Israel sparks accusations of Netanyahu-fuelled incitement
stories.summary: A fire at a mosque in the Arab village of Ed-Dahi near Afula, daubed with "revenge" graffiti, drew condemnation from Arab and Jewish lawmakers who blamed Netanyahu's rhetoric against Arab citizens, coming hours after a car-ramming attack wounded several people in Kafr Qasim.

stories.headline: Iraq strikes compromise with Iran-backed Kataib Hezbollah
stories.summary: Baghdad's attempt to reclaim a militia stronghold could test the government's authority over armed factions while leaving much of Tehran's political and economic influence in Iraq intact, experts told Iran International, after PM Ali al-Zaidi readied forces before reaching the deal.

stories.headline: West presses Iran at IAEA to resume inspections of bombed nuclear sites
stories.summary: The US, Britain, France and Germany jointly pressed Tehran at the UN atomic watchdog's board meeting to allow inspectors access to nuclear sites hit in last year's military strikes.

stories.headline: ICJ rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
stories.summary: The World Court's first-ever genocide ruling against a state, over Myanmar's treatment of the Rohingya Muslim minority, is being closely watched by regional outlets, with analysts noting it could complicate Israel's defence against South Africa's Gaza genocide case.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: No recent Middle East-beat coverage was found from Gulf News, Saudi Gazette, Al Arabiya English or The New Arab beyond a passing mention in another outlet's reporting.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Coverage this week centers on Sudan's unraveling RSF leadership facing justice, major African economic diplomacy around IMF deals and investment pipelines, and significant mining-sector moves from Angola's diamond ambitions to an Ebola scare at a DRC gold mine. Tech and telecoms investment -- from US giants eyeing Cape Town to MTN's Central African expansion -- also features prominently.

stories.headline: Sudan court hands RSF leader Hemedti second death sentence over $396 million scandal
stories.summary: A Port Sudan court sentenced RSF commander Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as Hemedti, along with his two brothers and 11 others, to death for a second time over a massive corruption scandal.

stories.headline: Egypt secures $2.3 billion IMF deal as economic recovery gains momentum
stories.summary: Egypt struck a new $2.3 billion IMF agreement as GDP growth hit 5.1 percent in the 2025-2026 fiscal year, buoyed by tourism, manufacturing and other sectors.

stories.headline: Tech giants flock to Cape Town as Washington shuns Pretoria
stories.summary: Amazon, Google, Meta, OpenAI, Microsoft, Oracle, SpaceX and Starlink are set to attend the African Tech festival in Cape Town even after the Trump administration stripped South Africa of its AGOA trade access; Africa Confidential is a subscription newsletter whose reporting reflects its own insider sourcing rather than an official position.

stories.headline: Angola seeks 10% stake in De Beers under Anglo's proposed exit
stories.summary: A mines ministry spokesperson told Reuters that Angola is seeking a 10% holding in De Beers as part of Anglo American's planned sale of its stake in the diamond producer.

stories.headline: African regional governments prep $9.5bn investment pipeline
stories.summary: African Business reports regional governments are assembling a multi-billion-dollar investment pipeline, part of broader coverage of AfDB president Sidi Ould Tah's first year in office and efforts to close Africa's financing gap.

stories.headline: In Rabat, US envoy Mike Waltz sets out next steps for Western Sahara
stories.summary: On a tour of Lebanon and Morocco, US UN representative Mike Waltz reaffirmed Washington's backing for resolving the Western Sahara dispute through Moroccan autonomy.

stories.headline: Telecom towers: MTN clears hurdle in Central African IHS takeover
stories.summary: The CEMAC telecoms regulator gave conditional approval to MTN's acquisition of IHS towers, though MTN must still submit terms to reassure rival operators, especially in Cameroon.

Africa.gaps: The Continent's site returned only older archived issues with no stories from the last 48 hours, so nothing current could be confirmed from that outlet. Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT and WSJ block direct search and had no relevant items in the provided feed, so their current Africa coverage could not be assessed beyond what appeared via other outlets' citations of Reuters.

Media.overview: Coverage across media-industry outlets is dominated by labor unrest over AI and wages at Reuters, press-freedom flashpoints tied to Trump's Asia trip and Russell Brand's conviction, and the continuing economic upheaval facing local and legacy newsrooms. Trade outlets are also tracking business maneuvering in streaming/FAST platforms and entertainment deal-making.

stories.headline: Reuters journalists authorize strike over AI protections and wages
stories.summary: Nearly 96% of roughly 300 unionized Reuters journalists in the U.S. voted to authorize a strike after more than a year of bargaining, with disputes centered on wage increases that lag inflation and demands for a share of revenue from AI licensing deals and human oversight of AI-generated content.

stories.headline: Press freedom clashes mark Trump's Asia trip, including phone seizures and a reporter booted from China summit
stories.summary: U.S. authorities confiscated phones from reporters traveling with Trump as he left China after the APEC summit, while separately a Bloomberg reporter was ejected from the summit after shouting a question about Jensen Huang, and a Fox reporter publicly lamented that Chinese journalists 'do not enjoy freedom of the press.'

stories.headline: UK government pressures Google to remove Russell Brand's YouTube channel after rape conviction; Google refuses
stories.summary: Google declined a UK government request to pull a YouTube video in which Russell Brand's wife read a statement maintaining his innocence after his rape conviction, even as the UK culture minister made an emotional public plea for the channel's removal and Meta has already restricted his other accounts.

stories.headline: Newsmax sues Fox over Roku deal, alleging antitrust violation
stories.summary: Newsmax filed an antitrust lawsuit alleging that Fox's ownership stakes in Tubi and The Roku Channel give it roughly 71% control of the U.S. FAST (free ad-supported streaming TV) market.

stories.headline: McClatchy plans to rebuild its newsrooms around AI after mass layoffs
stories.summary: Two months after laying off more than 90 journalists, McClatchy executives offered a blunt assessment that the storied local newspaper chain's future will be built around AI.

stories.headline: Egyptian government brings court case against Mada Masr editor Lina Attalah
stories.summary: Lina Attalah, editor of Egypt's most prominent independent outlet Mada Masr, is being taken to court by her government, and says despite remaining hopeful, 'journalism cannot breathe' under the current crackdown.

stories.headline: Kyiv Independent eyes expansion beyond Ukraine coverage
stories.summary: Five years after launch, the Kyiv Independent now has a 100-strong team and roughly $4 million in annual revenue, and is positioning itself for a broader role beyond Ukraine in what it calls an 'age of confrontation.'

stories.headline: Puck's Dylan Byers examines Bulwark publisher Sarah Longwell's reluctance to sell despite investment interest
stories.summary: Puck's media vertical reports that Bulwark publisher Sarah Longwell's Never Trump-aligned outlet is on track for $30 million in revenue this year, yet she appears reluctant to sell even as the media environment looks ripe for investment.

Media.gaps: No outlet-specific search results were available for NYT, WSJ, FT, or The Guardian since those outlets block web search and no feed items were provided for them; Status's web presence surfaced only older archived stories rather than items from the last 24-48 hours.
